details: On May 20, 2026, former President Trump issued an executive order directing the Federal Reserve to evaluate expanding direct access to its payment systems for fintech and crypto firms. Subsequently, the Fed proposed "payment accounts" for eligible non-bank financial institutions, offering limited access to clearing and settlement services to foster innovation while mitigating risks.
title: Trump Order Spurs Fed Review of Crypto Payment Access

details: A consortium, Qivalis, now backed by 37 European banks, plans to launch a fully regulated, 1:1 euro-backed stablecoin in the second half of 2026. This initiative aims to establish a European alternative to current dollar-dominated stablecoins, facilitating efficient cross-border payments and digital asset settlements under MiCA regulations.
title: 37 European Banks Back Euro Stablecoin Project by Qivalis

details: Bitcoin prices surged on May 24, 2026, recovering from recent lows, after former US President Donald Trump announced a "largely negotiated" peace agreement with Iran, which includes the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. This de-escalation of geopolitical tensions is widely seen as a positive development for global risk assets, including Bitcoin.
title: Bitcoin Rallies as Trump Announces "Largely Negotiated" Iran Deal

details: Markets are keenly awaiting several crucial US economic data releases this week. These include the Consumer Confidence Index (Tuesday, May 26), Q1 2026 GDP figures (Thursday, May 28), and April PCE inflation data (Friday, May 29). These reports are significant as they will inform Federal Reserve policy expectations, with potential implications for interest rates and overall market risk appetite.
title: Key US Economic Data to Influence Crypto Markets This Week

details: Digital asset investment products experienced significant net outflows of $1.07 billion for the week ending May 18, 2026, with Bitcoin funds seeing $982 million in redemptions, attributed largely to geopolitical risk aversion related to Iran. However, a January 2026 survey by Coinbase and EY-Parthenon indicates that nearly three-quarters of institutional investors plan to increase their crypto allocations this year, driven by regulatory clarity and improved infrastructure.
title: Crypto Funds See $1.07B Outflows; Institutions Remain Long-Term Bullish
